title: Which game engines are you all using for your games?
author: Patient-Software-168
selftext: I am currently using Godot for a sim rts game, and was wondering what everyone else uses for their AI game made projects.

comments.author: Denaton_
comments.body: None, I realized that today's AI is powerful enough to design the engine around the game instead of designing the game around the engine.

replies.author: eugene20
replies.body: Look at Mr moneybags here :D

replies.author: Charming_You_25
replies.body:
I’ve been experimenting for the past year building a text based game engine/kernal on a relational graph database. Allowing the underlying engine to work with natural language has provided some interesting opportunities. It started off as a way so the engine could use llms for black box function calls (example: generate this item’s stats, or, what does the user’s input text mean in engine terms). But, given the amount of things that need to be computed for a cohesive experience figuring out non-llm tricks has turned out to be super fruitful. Like, stepping relational ontologies is fast and basically a free op. For example if i need to understand what rust is and what it does to a sword, i dont need an llm call if i already know what the sword is and what it’s made of. (Rust>corrosion>**reduced durability and edge**)(short sword>one handed arms>**weapon**)=(lower weapon damage and chance of breaking on use)

I’m now seeing a path where I could use the same engine to drive a 3d with natural language using text to motion, text to object, text to placement, eventually without llm calls at all once all the primitives are defined. If I built that part now, I’d probably use three.js/webgpu but, i suspect once Gaussian splats come a little further and allow animation and collision things could get WILD with a custom engine.

replies.author: Own_Badger6076
replies.body: You have full control over the engines capabilities if you're the one making it. It might take longer, but if you're in it for the long haul it's worthwhile.

replies.author: _Fauxpaw
replies.body:
A premade engine is good because you already know the game will work on multiple different platforms and configurations. When you make your own engine, they tend to get tuned for your specific computer's parameters, and then you're wondering why someone with a different video card is getting wildly different results from you.

How do you avoid that problem?

replies.author: SmartCustard9944

I’m also against limitations. I just want to point out that even with a beefy PC, due to concurrent AI agents working it is constantly maxed out, which means I need to anyway start distributing my local compute across multiple computers.

Perhaps people sticking with Unity can look into remote development on multiple computers.

comments.author: NooneLikesYouBill
comments.body:
I’ve used Unity since it went free back in 2015 (iirc? Can’t remember now, it was on my radar already but slashdot posted an article about free licenses and I was hooked).

No longer using Unity: the runtime fee, killing hdrp, now probably being bought by the EA/Saudis (nothing against the Saudis, just reflecting what they did to EA)..

Tried Godot for a bit and it works really well with AI esp local AI (gdscript), but the quality just isn’t there for me yet. I left Unity over losing hdrp, Godot is nowhere close \*yet.

Now on Unreal where I should have been all along. I want high quality and realistic graphics; never been into stylized or casual games, I grew up in the 80s had my fill of that decades ago. Really happy with Unreal 5.9p2 and the direction it’s headed. I know purists hate it, but meh, they’ve had their run.

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
[Breakout in a Destructible Material World | Metalrain Engine Showcase](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=waXkuklrtN4)

I built my own engine, the games are written in a programming language made for them (.mrgraph) and executed on the GPU. Right now it's optimizing for my phone. Engine is written in rust from scratch.

Can package windows/linux/mac/android right now, ios and web will come soon. iOS is easy, web is a bit of a pain since I need to drop all async and be single threaded, but it's possible.
